anthocyanins are promising natural anti-inflammatory molecules, but the action mechanisms and efficacy of anthocyanin-containing extracts as compared to established drugs still require clarification.

ARF, in spite of being a very low dose, showed a strong anti-inflammatory activity, as compared with 5-ASA in the TNBS-induced colitic rats, and that such activity is mainly due to the downregulation of COX- 2, iNOS and leukocyte infiltration and the increase in antioxidant defenses.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
anthocyanins may have a higher anti-inflammatory action than 5-aminosalicilic acid in a rat model of colitis.
the anthocyanin fraction from blueberries showed a higher anti-inflammatory action than 5-aminosalicilic acid (5- ASA), a first-line anti-inflammatory drug for inflammatory bowel disease.
anthocyanins may be considered a promising natural alternative in IBD management, and the use of ARF, as a whole, may be more effective than the use of individual anthocyanins.

anthocyanins from blueberries are able to exert a significant anti-inflammatory effect on colitis in a rat model, which was comparable or even higher than 5-aminosalicilic acid, a first-line anti-inflammatory drug in IBD.
